$comment: Felling (docs/FELLING.md §5): what loses its support falls as a body, tips and settles back into blocks. riderReach: how far (cells, through leaves) a leaf belongs to the log nearest it. maxSystemCells: the most logs and leaves one support search looks at (a larger tree stands). maxPieceCells: the most cells one falling piece may have. toppleSpin: the spin (rad/s) a piece cut by a player starts with, tipping it away from them about its foot; toppleTipSpeed: at most this fast (m/s) at its farthest point, so a tall trunk is nudged, not flung. sleepLinear / sleepAngular / restDrift: a piece slower than these (m/s, rad/s), or that has not gone farther than restDrift (m, at its farthest point) since it began counting (jostled in a heap of pieces, rocked by water), for sleepSeconds settles; the pieces due settle together every settleEveryTicks server ticks (60 a second): one modification and one terrain-collision rebuild a chunk for all that settle then, not one each tick. maxSeconds: a piece still moving after this settles where it is. maxSettles: a piece that has settled this many times stays where it settles, anchored or not (1: what lands falls no further; owner, 2026-11-02). hitSpeed: a piece hitting a player faster than this (m/s, its speed toward them) hurts, hitDamagePerSpeed points per m/s over it. holdSpeed: a piece slower than this (m/s, at any point) is held from players' contacts and moved by their push instead (the controller's maxPushForce over its mass a tick, toward their speed into it; the clients predict the same: docs/BUILT_BODIES.md §6, owner 2026-11-02); faster, it moves as the physics says (held fast, a falling piece would squeeze players through the ground). pushHoldSeconds: a pushed piece stays held this long after its last push, however fast. settleGlideSeconds: how long (s) a settling piece is drawn gliding from where it rests into its blocks' places (and a cell moved at settling, from where it would have gone), on the clients only. settleBounce: how far past its place (a fraction of the glide) it swings before it rests. terrainChunksPerTick: the most terrain-collision chunks the server builds a tick round falling pieces (their bounds, nearest first): a long piece's ground loads over a few ticks rather than stalling one. Run `node shared/physics/gen.mjs` after editing; CI fails if crates/dwell-sim/src/felling.gen.rs is stale.
